top_signal.title: I know pool service cold but not marketing. How do I go from 3 clients to 100 without a referral network?
top_signal.summary: I run a small residential pool service company in Florida. I've been in the industry since 2020. I'm a state-certified Certified Pool Operator, fully insured, and I own my truck and equipment outright.  The technical side is my strength. I balance water using the Langelier Saturation Index (LSI) instead of just checking chlorine and pH. I document every visit, and I tell customers what I did and why. The result is clean water, protected equipment, and no surprises.  My problem is the other half of the business. I have 3 independent clients and I want to get to around 100. I don't know how to get there.  The usual advice is to start with friends, family, and neighbors and let referrals snowball. I can't do that. I'm building in an area where I don't have a personal network yet, so I have no circle of friends to tap and no word of mouth to ride.   What I have so far:   A live website  A Google Business Profile  Business cards  A dedicated business phone line  Three happy clients, one of whom found me almost by accident   What I'd love help with:   If you built a local service business from near zero without a referral base, what got you your first 20 to 30 customers?  Should Google Business Profile get most of my effort early on? What moved the needle for you there?  How do you build reviews and a reputation with only a handful of customers?  What do you wish you'd known when you had 3 customers?  I'm not looking for a growth hack. I'd rather grow slowly and do it right. I'm no
